messages:
taylor: FYI alert — p95 latency jumped ~3x on eu-dedicated at 09:12 UTC, sustained ~3m. console shows scale policy firing repeatedly.

infra-bot: [ALERT] cluster/eu-dedicated p95_tokens 1200ms -> 3800ms at 2026-03-17T09:12:04Z. autoscaler: scale-up initiated (x3). link: https://console.redwood.example/alerts/12345

maria: seeing a lot of 502s from grpc-proxy? Any noisy tenants?

eugene: checking logs — high KV cache miss rate across nodes, eviction rate spiked. suspect cache thrash after a rolling deployment at 09:08.

lena: flamegraph from perf shows hot path waiting on `kv_lookup` + `gpu_fill_zero` (weird). paste: 
```
45.3% kv_lookup
20.1% gpu_fill_zero
12.4% batch_pack
8.7% kernel_selector_slowpath
```

chris: kernel selector falling back to CPU fallback on some nodes due to missing CUDA lib on image? image tag shows `r-infer:v20260317-rolling`.

maria: confirmed — node-image mismatch on subset of autoscaled nodes: missing optimized kernels, falling back to slower kernels. that explains big p95.

taylor: but we also saw large batches forming — batch window jumped from ~10ms to 150ms. ops-bot: rate of requests didn't change.

eugene: hypothesis: cache misses cause longer per-request time -> batching heuristics absorb more requests -> bigger batches -> slow kernel path increases latency -> autoscaler sees latency and keeps scaling up -> new nodes missing optimized libs -> more slow nodes: feedback loop.

maria: rolling back that deployment fixed missing libs? any quick mitigation?

lena: immediate mitigations i) drain new nodes via `kubectl annotate node ...` ii) force kernel selector to prefer fallback quantized kernel that exists on all nodes `REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=quantized_v1` iii) reduce batch window to 20ms on route `/v1/generate`.

taylor: doing i and iii now. also enabling route-level circuit that routes heavy embedding tenants to dedicated smaller batch model.

infra-bot: [CMD] kubectl cordon node/gpu-23

chris: after cordon, p95 dropping to ~950ms. but autoscaler still at +x2 instances; provisioning lag because nodes are brand new and image pulls are slow (~2m).

eugene: profiling after mitigation shows kv_hit_rate back to normal but kernel_selector microsecond penalty still present on scaled nodes. need image fix.

maria: created hotfix image with missing kernel libs: `r-infer:v20260317-hotfix-kernels`. start rolling now.

taylor: rolling update triggered, will prefer reusing warm cache nodes first.

lena: proposal for postmortem actions:
- make autoscaler backoff avoid immediate re-scaling while image mismatch detected
- add preflight image-kernel check during node boot
- make batcher aware of KV miss-rate to reduce window when miss-rate spikes
- reserve a tiny warm pool of validated nodes for bursts

eugene: adding perf test to CI that verifies kernel_selector chooses expected kernels for each image.

maria: QA: reproduce by simulating KV eviction via `redis-cli FLUSHALL` on a node and running load. test script in repo: `tools/repro/kv-thrash.sh`.

taylor: good. owners: infra (image fix) = chris, runtime batching/selector = lena, postmortem writeup = eugene. I'll ping support for customer comms.

ops-bot: incident severity P2 -> created incident 2026-03-17-eviction-scale-loop.

chris: image fixed and nodes are back to optimized kernel. p95 now ~220ms. closing mitigation window.

taylor: thanks everyone. we'll put a short postmortem and action items in #postmortems. :thumbsup:
